act.selectedObject: A Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints house-of-worship occurrence under the bounded non-reciprocal-imposition condition
act.speakingGrain: The Church’s published scriptures, published repentance teaching, observable institutional record, and the affected site record
act.boundary: No divine voice, no inferred private mental state, no blanket verdict, no detached conclusion
act.requestedOutcome: A neutral public article, addressable field, recorded act, and ledger

nodes.title: The bounded condition
nodes.statement: A church institution establishes or maintains a house of worship after directly affected people have refused the specific imposition, and the institution has not resolved the harm through genuine consent, departure, or repair.
nodes.remainder: For any named site, establish the affected parties, direct effects, exact refusal, available alternatives, institutional knowledge, continuation, and repair.

nodes.title: The speaking grain
nodes.statement: The speaker is the retained religious and institutional grain: published Church scripture, published Church teaching, and observable Church acts. This record does not speak as God or infer divine intent.

nodes.title: Reciprocity root
nodes.statement: The Church’s published scripture directs a person to do to others what that person would have others do to them and identifies that rule with the law and the prophets.
nodes.remainder: Application to a particular land-use occurrence requires the complete factual record.

nodes.title: Observable repentance test
nodes.statement: Within the Church’s published grain, repentance requires confession and forsaking; its published teaching also requires repair of hurt or damage where possible.
nodes.remainder: A public record can test observable cessation and repair, not private belief or divine forgiveness.

nodes.title: Institutional site act
nodes.statement: The relevant act includes acquisition, design, application, negotiation, construction, maintenance, and the directly produced effects at the selected site.
nodes.remainder: Resolve each act and actor from the site record; do not collapse the institution into every member.

nodes.title: Conditional theological finding
nodes.statement: If the Church knowingly continues a specific non-reciprocal imposition on directly affected people and neither forsakes nor repairs the established wrong, the continuing church occurrence is the continuing breach. Within the Church’s own classification, it is a sin carried on in the name of the religious grain the institution claims to obey.
nodes.remainder: The conclusion attaches only after every factual condition is established for the named occurrence.

nodes.title: Fairview public state
nodes.statement: The public records establish opposition, mediation, changes to the proposal, Town Council approval, construction, and continued disagreement.
nodes.remainder: The reviewed records do not alone establish unresolved non-reciprocal imposition after complete comparison of effects, affected parties, authority, alternatives, consent, and repair.

nodes.title: Fairview verdict
nodes.statement: The conditional theological finding cannot yet be attached to Fairview as a complete verdict from the reviewed public sources.
nodes.remainder: FIRST_MISSING_REFERENCE: a complete, reconciled site-level evidence record for direct effects, affected-party boundary, exact refusal, reciprocal alternatives, institutional knowledge, and repair after the mediated approval.
